title: Rory and the Lunchtime Whistle
markdown:
Rory the rooster was a lovely fellow. His comb was a soft, rosy red, and his morning crow was as dependable as the morning light. But Rory loved his lunchtime best of all. He knew, right down to the exact moment, when it was time to eat, not just by the warm sun high above, but by the gentle rumble in his own happy tummy. And it was precisely at this lunchtime, when the sun was warm and the midday bell was about to ring, that Rory heard a sound. A soft, reedy whistle, like a whispered tune, coming from beneath the barn floorboards. *Wheeeet, wheeeet!* it would drift, a questioning little melody that floated up as he thought of warm grains and lovely, tender worms.

At first, Rory thought it was a dream, or perhaps the wind playing amongst the straw. But the whistle was always there, a sweet little song that came with his hunger. He would tilt his head, his bright, round eye looking at the worn wooden planks, and wonder. This simply wouldn’t do. A mystery, especially one that happened so softly at lunchtime, needed a little gentle exploring.

So, Rory, with a soft flap of his wings, went to find his dearest friend, Lark the lamb. Lark was the softest, fluffiest lamb you could ever imagine, like a little woolly cloud, with large, gentle eyes that held a quiet calm. Her bleat was more like a soft sigh, and she had a way of making any little worry feel lighter. “Lark, my dear woolly friend,” Rory whispered, his voice full of a gentle curiosity. “There is a matter of gentle importance that needs your calm wisdom. A sound, a peculiar little whistle, that appears right at lunchtime, from beneath the barn. It’s a little puzzle, Lark, and puzzles are meant to be solved, aren’t they?”

Lark, who was peacefully nibbling on sweet clover near the old oak tree, blinked her large, innocent eyes, her soft nose twitching. “A whistle, Rory? That does sound very curious. I will help you find it, of course. Where shall we begin our quiet looking?” Her voice was as soft as her wool, full of gentle reassurance.

Rory, ever so pleased, led Lark to the grand old barn. The late morning sun cast long, lazy shadows across the straw. He showed her the spot where the sound seemed to come from, a cluster of slightly looser floorboards near the back wall. They listened together, their heads tilted in quiet expectation. *Wheeeet, wheeeet!* There it was again, clear as a drop of morning dew. Rory, with his sturdy legs, gently nudged one of the loose floorboards. It wiggled softly. Lark, with her patient nudges, used her soft head to help. Slowly, with a soft, protesting creak, the board lifted, revealing not just dusty earth and tangled roots, but a small, dark opening.

“Oh my!” whispered Lark, her woolly ears twitching with surprise and wonder. “It’s a little hole! What’s down there, Rory? It looks like a little secret way.”

Rory peered into the opening, his bright eyes looking into the dimness. It wasn’t just a hole; it looked like a little tunnel, lined with something smooth. He gently pecked at the edge, and as he did, a bit more of the board gave way, revealing a series of small, neat passages carved into the earth. It was an old vent system, long forgotten, a hidden network beneath their feet! And nestled in the soft dust, glinting faintly in the light, was a small, tarnished tin whistle.

Rory carefully nudged it out with his beak. It was old, very old, its metal worn smooth by time. Lark sniffed it gently, her whiskers tickling its surface. “It’s a whistle, Rory,” she confirmed softly. “Like the sound you heard. It must be the source of the mystery!”

“Indeed, Lark! But why would someone hide a whistle here? And why only at lunchtime?” Rory wondered aloud, tapping his beak thoughtfully. He looked around the old barn, his mind wandering to the farm’s past, remembering stories his Grandpa rooster had told him about old Farmer Giles and his scruffy, very sleepy dog named Buster. Buster, Grandpa said, loved naps more than anything.

“Ah, but here’s the lovely part, my dear Lark,” Rory said, a bright understanding dawning in his eyes, like the gentle sunrise. “Buster the dog, he loved his naps. And where did he love to nap best, on a warm day? Right here, under the barn, where it was cool and beautifully dark for a good snooze!” Rory looked at the tarnished tin whistle, then back at the little vent. “And Farmer Giles, when it was lunchtime and Buster was too sound asleep to hear the dinner bell, Farmer Giles would come to this very spot, by the loose floorboard, and blow this very whistle! *Wheeeet, wheeeet!* he’d gently toot, a special signal so Buster would wake up from his deep slumber and amble out for his meal.”

Lark let out a soft, understanding bleat, her fluffy tail swaying gently. “So, the whistle was to wake up Buster for his lunch! That’s very clever, Rory. A little secret helper for a napping dog.”

Rory puffed out his chest, his red comb glowing with quiet pride. He felt very wise. “It is indeed. A hidden helper for a sleepy dog who loved his naps. And now, the mystery is solved, tucked away like a smooth, round pebble.” He looked at the old whistle, now resting safely beside him, and then at Lark. “It’s a good thing we found it, though. All that napping must have been very peaceful for Buster. I imagine he dreamt of many lovely, warm things.”

The sun was beginning its slow, golden descent towards the horizon, painting the sky in soft hues of rose and lavender, a gentle sign that the day was winding down. The lunchtime whistle had long since faded, replaced by the soft, rhythmic chirping of evening crickets and the low cooing of doves settling into the eaves. Rory and Lark, their gentle adventure finished, their puzzle solved, felt a deep sense of calm wash over them. They nestled together near the barn door, the warm straw a soft cushion for their tired bodies, and watched the fireflies begin their slow, twinkling dance, like tiny fallen stars waking up. Their whole little adventure had been a quiet one, a gentle uncovering of a small, old secret, as soft as moonlight on a meadow. And as the last rays of warm sun kissed their sleepy faces, they knew it was time for rest. Rory gave a contented little cluck, a sound full of sleepy satisfaction, and Lark let out a soft, sleepy sigh, snuggling closer. Everything was just right on Sunny Meadow Farm, and soon, with the peaceful quiet of the evening settling all around them, they both drifted off into a deep, contented slumber, ready for sweet dreams.
characters: Rory the rooster, Lark the lamb
